subject: Private VPC: egress patterns, control plane handshake, and reference diagrams
messages:
From: Alex Hudson <alex.hudson@novacorp.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <p.singh@novacorp.com>
Date: 2027-02-14T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Private VPC: initial ask — control plane egress and reference diagrams

Hi Soojin,

Quick context: we (NovaCorp infra) are evaluating Redwood Private for a customer-facing inference workload that must live in our AWS VPCs. Two immediate asks before we kick off procurement:

1) A concise reference diagram that shows the control plane <-> data plane interaction (which endpoints need outbound egress, typical ports, and expected FQDNs).
2) An egress policy matrix: which Redwood services call home, whether we can use VPC endpoints, static IP ranges, or need NAT with SNAT; any support for private links.

Regulatory note: our auditors require minimal internet egress. Ideally the control plane signals can go to an allowlisted set or via a private interconnect.

Attaching our high-level infra requirements for reference (novacorp_infra_requirements.pdf). Would you be able to share a reference diagram and a short matrix? If helpful, we can schedule a 30-min technical handshake this week.

Thanks,
Alex Hudson
Director, Cloud Engineering — NovaCorp

Attachment: novacorp_infra_requirements.pdf (application/pdf, 420KB)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Alex Hudson <alex.hudson@novacorp.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <p.singh@novacorp.com>, dev.patel@redwood.com
Date: 2027-02-14T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private VPC: initial ask — control plane egress and reference diagrams

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear summary and the PDF.

We can absolutely provide both a diagram and an egress matrix. High level notes up front:
- Control plane traffic is primarily outbound TLS to our control plane endpoints (we can provide FQDNs and ASN ranges).
- Data plane (inference runtime) stays inside your VPC unless you opt into our hosted model catalog pulls; model artifacts can be staged via S3 in your account.
- We support allowlists and can provide an IP-range export; for stricter environments we have a private interconnect option (Direct Connect / PrivateLink) in some regions.

I'll draft a reference diagram and a short controlplane-egress-matrix and send them back for your review.
Can we do a technical handshake Thursday 2027-02-17 at 10:00 PT? If that works I’ll invite our infra and security engineers.

Action: looping in Dev (dev.patel), Evelyn (evelyn.hart), and Rishi (rishi.malhotra) to help with the diagram and the FQDN/IP outputs.

Cheers,
Soojin Lee
Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: dev.patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, evelyn.hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, rishi.malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-15T09:18:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: draft reference diagram + questions for NovaCorp

Team — pulling together the draft attached (redwood_private_reference_diagram_v1.png). Notes and open questions:

Summary in the diagram:
- Control plane (managed by Redwood) runs in our control-plane cluster (hosted). Control plane endpoints accept outbound TLS-only connections from the customer VPC for lifecycle calls, telemetry, and certificate renewal.
- Data plane (customer-owned) runs in NovaCorp VPC: inference pods on EC2/GPU nodes. KVS and model cache remain inside the VPC.
- Optional model artifact staging: customers can host model artifacts in their S3 and we pull via presigned URLs, or Redwood can push artifacts into a customer bucket with cross-account role.

Open questions we need to confirm with NovaCorp:
1) Do they allow outbound connections to FQDN-based allowlists, or do we need fixed egress IPs?
2) Are VPC endpoints allowed for S3 / STS / ECR (we can avoid internet egress iff endpoints are present)?
3) Do they want control plane telemetry to be proxied via an internal egress gateway (their side)?

Requested deliverables for the Thursday 10:00 PT handshake:
- Control plane FQDNs and ports (I’ll bring a draft list).
- Egress matrix (controlplane-egress-matrix.xlsx) showing protocol, port, direction, fallback.
- A short checklist for procurement/network (static routes, NAT behavior, TLS inspection notes).

Please review the attached diagram and update any technical callouts.

Thanks — Soojin
---
Attachment: controlplane-egress-matrix.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 18KB)

From: Alex Hudson <alex.hudson@novacorp.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <p.singh@novacorp.com>
Date: 2027-02-17T10:46:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private VPC: egress patterns, control plane handshake, and reference diagrams

Thanks for the diagram and matrix — that helped. A few clarifications from our side after the call:

1) Allowlist approach: auditors prefer minimal internet egress. We can provision a small set of NAT egress IPs (static) for outbound to Redwood control plane FQDNs; alternatively we can use a proxy that does TLS passthrough and allowlist FQDNs. IP-based allowlisting is preferred.
2) VPC endpoints: we plan to enable Gateway endpoints for S3 and Interface endpoints for STS/ECR. That should avoid model artifact pulls from traversing the internet.
3) TLS inspection: not allowed for outbound to Redwood control plane (must be end-to-end TLS).

I've attached our current egress whitelist export (nova_egress_whitelist.csv) which includes the NAT IPs we can allocate.

Next steps we’d like from Redwood:
- Finalized reference diagram with explicit arrows labeled "control plane egress (TLS)" and a short one-page egress checklist we can hand to our network team.
- A concise statement of whether Redwood supports static egress IP ranges (yes/no) and how those are maintained during failover.

If you can get the updated diagram and the one-pager by Friday EOD (2027-02-19) we can circulate to procurement.

Best,
Alex

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Alex Hudson <alex.hudson@novacorp.com>
Cc: dev.patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, evelyn.hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, rishi.malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Priya Singh <p.singh@novacorp.com>
Date: 2027-02-19T16:41:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private VPC: finalized artifacts and next steps

Alex / Priya — thanks for the call and for the whitelist. Attached are the deliverables you requested:

1) redwood_private_reference_diagram_v1.png (updated): arrows clearly labeled for control plane egress, data plane local traffic, and optional model staging flows.
2) controlplane-egress-matrix.xlsx (final): includes FQDNs, recommended ports (443/TCP), presence of CDN endpoints, and recommended fallback (PrivateLink / NAT).
3) one-page egress checklist (inlined below) for your network team.

One-page checklist (copy/paste friendly):
- Provide static NAT egress IPs that will be allowlisted on the Redwood control plane. If static IPs are not possible, confirm FQDN-based allowlisting and note that DNS-based allowlists require DNS stability.
- Enable S3 Gateway and STS/ECR Interface endpoints to avoid internet egress for model pulls.
- Ensure TLS passthrough; do not terminate TLS for control plane endpoints.
- Confirm KMS cross-account role if Redwood will push model artifacts into customer S3 (we included role template in Confluence).
- Schedule port tests: outbound 443 to redwood-control-*.redwood.ai and to redwood-metrics.redwood.ai on test day.

Static egress IPs: Redwood can provide a published set of IP ranges for control plane egress in a maintenance window; however, during certain DR failovers the specific source IP may change. We commit to publishing a list and giving 48 hours notice for planned changes; for hard restrictions we recommend a private interconnect (Direct Connect / PrivateLink).

Action items and owners:
- (Redwood) Dev to export final FQDN list and scheduled test window — owner: dev.patel — due 2027-02-22.
- (NovaCorp) Alex / Priya to provision NAT/static IPs or confirm PrivateLink decision — due 2027-02-24.
- (Both) Schedule validation run (connectivity + model load) w/c 2027-03-01.

Linking artifacts: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Private+VPC+Reference+Deploy and shared Drive ref: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3c-redwood-ref-diagram

If that timeline works I’ll open a HubSpot record for tracking (HUBSPOT:deal_84721) and we’ll move to a scoped SOW.

Thanks — talk soon.

Soojin Lee
Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference
